message.content:
The function writes `n` bytes plus a NUL terminator at `dst[n]`, but never checks that `desc->offset + n` fits within the destination buffer. The bounds check on line 6 only validates against the input stream length, not the output slice capacity. The overflow is introduced by the write on line 10 (the NUL terminator past the end of the slice), which depends on the unchecked `n` from line 3 and the write on line 9.

The primary bug — writing past the end of the destination slice — is introduced at line 10 (the `dst[n] = '\0'` write), though line 9 also writes `n` bytes without a destination-size check. Since both writes lack a destination bounds check and are part of the same flawed logic, the smallest set covering the bug is lines 9 and 10.

Answer: 9,10
